headline: 30 banks hit as digital services suspended until Oct 10
summary: ATM, card, and digital transactions are disrupted for millions of users due to technical maintenance of the Q-Cash network.
details: Digital transactions across at least 30 banks have been severely disrupted after the Q-Cash payment switch, operated by IT Consultants (ITC), went offline for technical upgrades and system migration.
The disruption began on October 4 at 9 PM and is expected to continue until October 10 at 12 PM, leaving many cardholders unable to withdraw cash from ATMs.
Affected users are also facing issues with fund transfers, e-commerce payments, and international transactions, with some employees unable to withdraw their salaries.
Bangladesh Bank has summoned the Q-Cash management authority and ordered the immediate restoration of all switching card-related services to minimize customer suffering.
Banks that have their own independent switching systems alongside Q-Cash are still able to maintain card-based transactions, while those without alternatives are completely shut down.
The central bank clarified that transactions via the National Payment Switch Bangladesh (NPSB) platform, mobile financial services (MFS), and other payment systems remain operational.
caption:
Millions of bank users are stranded as 30 banks face a massive digital blackout. No ATMs, no transfers—until October 10.

Digital transactions across at least 30 banks have been severely disrupted after the Q-Cash payment switch, operated by IT Consultants (ITC), went offline for technical upgrades and system migration.

The disruption began on October 4 at 9 PM and is expected to continue until October 10 at 12 PM, leaving many cardholders unable to withdraw cash from ATMs.

Affected users are also facing issues with fund transfers, e-commerce payments, and international transactions, with some employees unable to withdraw their salaries.

Bangladesh Bank has summoned the Q-Cash management authority and ordered the immediate restoration of all switching card-related services to minimize customer suffering.

Banks that have their own independent switching systems alongside Q-Cash are still able to maintain card-based transactions, while those without alternatives are completely shut down.

The central bank clarified that transactions via the National Payment Switch Bangladesh (NPSB) platform, mobile financial services (MFS), and other payment systems remain operational.

headline_marked: Shoe garland hung on [[Bir Sreshtha Hamidur Rahman sculpture]] in Jhenaidah
headline: Shoe garland hung on Bir Sreshtha Hamidur Rahman sculpture in Jhenaidah
summary: Unknown persons desecrated the monument of the highest military honor recipient in the central bus terminal area, sparking widespread local anger.
details: Unknown people hung a garland of shoes on a sculpture of Bir Sreshtha Hamidur Rahman in Jhenaidah. The incident occurred at the under-construction monument located in the central bus terminal area.
Photos of the desecrated sculpture spread on social media on Tuesday morning, causing widespread anger among local residents.
The shoes were removed by midday on Tuesday, according to Kamaluzzaman, a leader of the district's Muktijoddha Sangsad.
Jhenaidah Sadar Police chief Md Asaduzzaman stated that police learned of the incident via Facebook and have launched an investigation.
District Commissioner Md Noman Hossain held a meeting in the evening and instructed police to take legal action against the perpetrators.
Bir Sreshtha Hamidur Rahman, a native of Jhenaidah, was posthumously awarded Bangladesh's highest military honor for his sacrifice in the 1971 Liberation War.
He was killed on October 28, 1971, in combat against Pakistani forces in Kamalganj, Moulvibazar.
